content:
General
* This is a nice little puzzle. Good job! It could arguably even be classified as a Clash of Code, although the requirement to implement a custom sort function makes it somewhat harder. I'd suggest requiring the minimum total penalty itself as an additional output. This would make the task slightly more substantial and, in my opinion, better suited as an Easy puzzle.

Goal
* Consider changing the second paragraph to specify 1-based indexing earlier:

For each assignment [[i]], where 1 ≤ [[i]] ≤ [[N]], [[Dᵢ]] is the number of days required to complete it, and [[Pᵢ]] is the penalty (in credits) incurred for each day it is overdue.

* In the third paragraph,

  • Please change "only work on" to "work on only".

  • Consider simplifying "Furthermore, once" to "Once".

* In the paragraph starting with "Determine", please add:

If multiple sequences produce the same minimum penalty, choose the lexicographically smallest sequence.

* Consider changing "Needed days to finish" to "Days required" to make the table heading sound more natural.

* Please add a full stop after "2 1 3".

* Please change "Late" to "Overdue" in the illustrative diagram for consistency with the terminology used elsewhere.

* The diagram looks very pretty and clear. However, the lines are long and could be cut off on narrow screens in the IDE view. Consider rotating the timeline by 90° so that the lines are shorter:

```
┌─◀
├─◀
├─┤
├─◀
├─┤
├─┤
├─◀
├─┤
├─┤
```
(and add the descriptions to the rotated version)

Output
* Please simplify this section to:

<<Line 1>>: The optimal sequence of assignments, represented by their 1-indexed positions and separated by single spaces.

Cases
* Please remove the trailing newline from the input for:
  • Harder Costlier Validator (Validator 3)
  • Some Long Term Tasks (Test 4)
  • Same (Test 6)
  • Some Critical Tasks (Test 7)
  • Some Critical Tasks Validator (Validator 7)

Thanks.
Good suggestions. All adopted. Thank you very much.
